But 'boiled in shared water' and 'no gluten-free handling is offered' are NOT — the article never mentions either, and a tourism blog is not where an absence-of-GF-handling claim can be evidenced. That is the one place a reader would expect airborne wheat flour and it is not wheat here; the record should say so rather than let 'flour is handled on-site' imply a wheat-dusted bench. (b) Tabelog records the former shop name as 「Odashi&Wheat isao」 — the wheat identity is in the shop's own history, worth a line.

Change 'bonito' to 'dried tuna flakes'. It matters to anyone avoiding a specific fish, and it is the same class of slip as a mistranslated ingredient.

quote: The bowls are built on a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare; brewed Japanese soy sauce typically contains wheat, and no wheat-free/tamari alternative is indicated.
found: 「こちらは、新メニューの黒醤油ラーメン。…複数の醤油をブレンドしたオリジナル醤油は、とてもまろやかな口あたり。」「こちらは白醤油ラーメン。」 Menu paragraph: 「定番ラーメンのほかに、黒醤油、白醤油、野菜たっぷりの香来麺、台湾ラーメン・まぜそば…つけ麺メニューもあります。餃子と唐揚げなどの一品や天津飯やチャーハンなどのごはんものも充実。」 Address block: 「元祖熟成細麺 香来 壬生本店／京都市中京区壬生馬場町35番地5」.

One of the two headline bowls is 白醤油ラーメン — white shoyu is brewed from a majority of WHEAT with only a small proportion of soy, i.e. more wheat-dominant than ordinary koikuchi, the exact opposite of tamari. A reader who has learned that 'white/light = less' could pick precisely the worst bowl here. Name 白醤油 explicitly. The same paragraph also lists 台湾まぜそば, つけ麺, 餃子, 唐揚げ and 天津飯 (starch-thickened sauce, usually soy-seasoned), so the wheat surface is the whole menu. found: Cited English menu: 「Ginjo Tsukemen Miso <No.1 Popular>… Small 160g / Regular 220g / Large 330g」, 「Meat Miso Ramen JPY 800」, 「Chicken Shoyu Ramen JPY 800」, 「Note: "Atsumori" and "Kae-Dama" are not available. Please be aware that the noodles take 15 minutes to cook.」 Japanese twin (公式): 「吟醸つけ麺 味噌」「肉味噌ラーメン」「鶏醤油ラーメン」, 更新日 2021/08/15.

method: 1 plain fetch of the cited /en/ menu page, then the Japanese s.tabelog.com/kyoto/A2601/A260101/26004660/dtlmenu/ to confirm identity and freshness; trading live (公式 page, ラーメン百名店 WEST 2025, no 閉店)
note: Right venue (Ginjo Ramen Kubota, 五条, 下京区西松屋町563) and the shoyu and miso bowls are on the page. Two corrections. (1) LOOK BOTH WAYS ON THE MISO: the record leans the gluten on 'miso tare … wheat-based soy sauce', but miso is not inherently wheat — 米味噌 and 豆味噌 are wheat-free (麦味噌 is barley, which is why the shop's type matters and is not published). Do not teach a reader that miso means wheat. (2) The certain, page-evidenced gluten is the NOODLES: this is a tsukemen house selling noodles by weight up to 330g with a 15-minute boil. Lead with that. Also flag freshness — the menu is stamped 更新日 2021/08/15 on both language versions, so it is five years stale even though the listing is 公式.

The record misses 煮玉子 (braised egg), a listed topping. And in the other direction, the honest statement is not 'nothing here is plant-based' but 'the only animal-free items are plain rice and 高菜ご飯' — say that, because a vegan travelling with a group can still sit down and eat rice. Rewrite as: meat-miso, chicken and dried-sardine items with an egg topping; no vegetable broth.

quote: No ingredient breakdown of the tare/soy sauce is published; standard ramen shoyu tare is wheat-based, so wheat should be assumed present.
found: The cited page never mentions soy sauce or a tare at all. It describes the broth as 「鴨と昆布のあっさり清湯スープです」 (duck and kombu clear soup) — and it DOES publish a noodle ingredient: 「麺はドイツ産ライ麦を使った風味豊かな全粒粉麺です」 and, for the tsukemen, 「ドイツ産のライ麦を練りこんだ平打ちの自家製麺。まるでパスタのような麺です」.
http: 200 (plain curl, iPhone UA). Corroboration: s.tabelog.com/kyoto/A2601/A260301/26031755/ 200; Ecosia 200 (Yahoo News expert article, 2026-07-29)
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page, 1 fetch of Tabelog with an iPhone UA, then Ecosia for the exact 全粒粉麺 wording (Yahoo Japan and the other engines were not needed)
note: SAFETY DEFECT, and it points the reader at the wrong grain. The claim rests on an assumed wheat shoyu tare while the page — and the shop's own current Tabelog blurb, 「麺は鴨の旨みに負けないよう、ドイツ産ライ麦を使った風味豊かな全粒粉麺を採用」, and a 2026-07-29 Yahoo News piece, 「麺は、ドイツ産ライ麦を使った自家製の全粒粉麺」 — state plainly that the noodles are German RYE wholemeal. Rye is one of the three gluten grains; this is documented, current, and certain, where the soy-sauce line is speculative and unevidenced. It matters doubly in Japan: ライ麦 is NOT on the statutory allergen list, so a celiac scanning a Japanese アレルギー表示 for 小麦 will find nothing and conclude the bowl is safe. Rewrite gf_cross_contamination to lead with the rye noodles and drop the tare speculation. gf_confidence 'no' is already correct — no tier change, only the reason changes.
